title: dimos robots
description: dimos/gateway/robots.json (generated) and robots.source.json (hand-written): every robot dimos supports, the directories its code lives in, and what each of its blueprints is for, with the settings to decide before running it.

types.description: The robot types, in the order a launcher groups robots by: each robot's `type` is one of these keys (or null: not a robot dimos drives, shown last under Other).

robots.description: Every robot, in display order, by id.

excluded.description: Directories under dimos/robot that are not robots, each with the reason.

global_config.description: robots.yaml only, generated: every GlobalConfig field with its type, default, choices and description, read from GlobalConfig (robots.json's settings take theirs from it).

type.description: What kind of robot it is: a key of the top-level `types` (dog, humanoid, wheeled, arm, drone), or null when it isn't a robot dimos drives (sensors, demos, simulators, coordinators). A launcher groups robots by it; Desktop's robot picker shows only the robots with a type.

manufacturer.description: Who makes it, as its `name` starts ("Unitree" for "Unitree Go2"); null for DIY, open-source and generic hardware, and for what isn't a robot. Robots in one vendor folder (dimos/robot/<vendor>/<robot>) share it.

dirs.description: The code directories that are this robot's (repo-relative). Every blueprint defined under one must be listed here.

recommended.description: The blueprints to suggest first for this robot, best first (a launcher lists them on top). Each is one of this robot's `blueprints`.

defaults.description: What a blueprint of this robot has unless it says otherwise.

blueprints.description: This robot's blueprints, by registered name (dimos/robot/all_blueprints.py).

description.description: one plain sentence or two: what it does and what it needs

starter.description: a pick for "start here": its rank (1 first) across every robot

hidden.description: a test, benchmark, mock or building block: listed only when asked for

recommended_config.description: The settings a person should decide before running it, in order (a launcher shows them with its Launch button, and a config editor puts them on top). Each names a config value (a GlobalConfig field `global`, or a module config field `module` + `field`), or is a pick of several values at once (a `label` and `choices` that each `set` some of them, e.g. Robot / Replay / Simulator). Any entry can have `choices` (an enum: segmented buttons for up to 4, else a select) and `when` (shown only while those config values hold). On a blueprint it replaces the robot's defaults' list; [] means none.

label.description: what to ask (robots.json: from GlobalConfig's field name unless the source names it); a pick's heading

kind.description: text (default), number, bool, or recording (a picker of dimos recordings)

docs.description: A page on how to find this value (where a robot's IP comes from); the Launcher links it beside the field. dimos/gateway/test_robots.py checks it resolves.

default.description: what to suggest: a value, or for a pick the label of the choice to start on (else its first)

choices.description: the options (an enum), each with a label: for a config value, each a `value` it can take; for a pick, each a `set` of config values (GlobalConfig field or <module>.<field> to its value) it applies together. Without `choices`: a free value.

when.description: show it only while these config values (GlobalConfig field or <module>.<field>, as some other entry sets them) are these, e.g. {"replay": true} for a recording picker

required.description: it won't run without it (while it is shown)

streams.description: recording: the streams it must have, each a list of acceptable names

nullable.description: generated: the GlobalConfig field takes null
